claim: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) is the leading cause of invasive bacterial neonatal infections.
source: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) is the leading cause of invasive bacterial neonatal infections.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citation to Edwards et al., 2011 in the introduction.

claim: Late-onset diseases (LOD) occur between 7 and 89 days of life.
source: Late-onset diseases (LOD) occur between 7 and 89 days of life
evidence: This is a standard clinical definition cited in the manuscript.

claim: LOD is largely due to the CC17 GBS hypervirulent clone.
source: Late-onset diseases (LOD) occur between 7 and 89 days of life and are largely due to the CC17 GBS hypervirulent clone.
evidence: This is supported by epidemiological data cited in the manuscript.

claim: E2-P4 C7 concentrations specifically favor CC17 GBS meningitis following mice oral infection.
source: we show that E2-P4 C7 concentrations specifically favor CC17 GBS meningitis following mice oral infection.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data showing higher bacterial counts in the brain of C7 mice compared to C0 and control mice.

claim: CC17 GBS crosses the intestinal barrier through M cells.
source: CC17 GBS crosses the intestinal barrier through M cells.
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy imaging and transcytosis assays showing bacterial association with M cells.

claim: The process of CC17 GBS crossing the intestinal barrier is mediated by the CC17-specific surface protein Srr2.
source: This process mediated by the CC17-specific surface protein Srr2
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments with ∆srr2 mutants showing reduced M cell association and transcytosis.

claim: E2-P4 C7 concentrations promote M cell differentiation.
source: E2-P4 C7 concentrations which promote M cell differentiation
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data showing increased levels of M cell differentiation markers in E2-P4 C7 condition.

claim: E2-P4 C7 concentrations enhance CC17 GBS invasiveness.
source: E2-P4 C7 concentrations which promote M cell differentiation and CC17 GBS invasiveness.
evidence: This is demonstrated by increased bacterial counts in various organs and enhanced transcytosis in E2-P4 C7 condition.

claim: GBS is a natural inhabitant of the gastrointestinal and vaginal flora of 10% to 30% healthy individuals.
source: Group B Streptococcus (Streptococcus agalactiae, GBS) is a natural inhabitant of the gastrointestinal and vaginal flora of 10% to 30% healthy individuals.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: GBS is a Gram positive encapsulated bacterium.
source: This Gram positive encapsulated bacterium
evidence: This is a basic microbiological characteristic of GBS.

claim: GBS neonatal infections have up to 10% mortality.
source: Despite appropriate antibiotic therapy, the global burden of GBS neonatal infections remains substantial, with up to 10% mortality and 30% neurologic sequelae in surviving infants (Libster et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Libster et al., 2012.

claim: GBS neonatal infections result in 30% neurologic sequelae in surviving infants.
source: Despite appropriate antibiotic therapy, the global burden of GBS neonatal infections remains substantial, with up to 10% mortality and 30% neurologic sequelae in surviving infants (Libster et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Libster et al., 2012.

claim: Early-onset disease (EOD) occurs within 48 hr after birth in 90% of the cases.
source: the early-onset disease (EOD) which occurs within 48 hr after birth in 90% of the cases
evidence: This is a standard clinical definition cited from Edwards et al., 2011.

claim: EOD primarily manifests as a pneumonia and a bacteremia subsequent to the inhalation by the neonate of GBS contaminated amniotic fluid or vaginal secretions during delivery.
source: EOD primarily manifests as a pneumonia and a bacteremia subsequent to the inhalation by the neonate of GBS contaminated amniotic fluid or vaginal secretions during delivery (Edwards et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Edwards et al., 2011.

claim: LOD is characterized by a bacteremia without focus and a high rate of associated meningitis.
source: the late-onset disease (LOD) which occurs between 7 and 89 days of life (Edwards et al., 2011). EOD primarily manifests as a pneumonia and a bacteremia subsequent to the inhalation by the neonate of GBS contaminated amniotic fluid or vaginal secretions during delivery (Edwards et al., 2011). In contrast, the mode of transmission and the infection route of LOD, characterized by a bacteremia without focus and a high rate of associated meningitis, remain elusive
evidence: This is a clinical characterization of LOD.

claim: The gastrointestinal tract represents the most likely portal of entry for LOD.
source: although the gastrointestinal tract represents the most likely portal of entry, the circumstances leading to LOD remain largely unknown (Tazi et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tazi et al., 2010.

claim: GBS strains are distributed among five major clonal complexes (CC).
source: Worldwide epidemiological data have identified that GBS strains are distributed among five major clonal complexes (CC) (Da Cunha et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Da Cunha et al., 2014.

claim: The hypervirulent CC17 clone is almost exclusively of capsular serotype III.
source: One particular GBS clone, almost exclusively of capsular serotype III and designated the hypervirulent CC17 clone
evidence: This is an established epidemiological characteristic.

claim: CC17 GBS is strongly associated with LOD (60% to 80% of the cases).
source: One particular GBS clone, almost exclusively of capsular serotype III and designated the hypervirulent CC17 clone, is strongly associated with LOD (60% to 80% of the cases) and with meningitis (approx. 80% of the cases) (Bekker et al., 2014; Jones et al., 2006; Joubrel et al., 2015; Seale et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: CC17 GBS is associated with meningitis in approximately 80% of the cases.
source: One particular GBS clone, almost exclusively of capsular serotype III and designated the hypervirulent CC17 clone, is strongly associated with LOD (60% to 80% of the cases) and with meningitis (approx. 80% of the cases) (Bekker et al., 2014; Jones et al., 2006; Joubrel et al., 2015; Seale et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: CC17 GBS expresses specific surface proteins which promote intestinal colonization.
source: CC17 GBS expresses specific surface proteins which promote intestinal colonization and confer blood brain barrier (BBB) translocation abilities in animal models (Six et al., 2015; Tazi et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Six et al., 2015 and Tazi et al., 2010.

claim: CC17 GBS expresses specific surface proteins which confer blood brain barrier (BBB) translocation abilities in animal models.
source: CC17 GBS expresses specific surface proteins which promote intestinal colonization and confer blood brain barrier (BBB) translocation abilities in animal models (Six et al., 2015; Tazi et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Six et al., 2015 and Tazi et al., 2010.

claim: CC17 GBS is less responsible for EOD.
source: Remarkably, this clone is less responsible for EOD and largely underrepresented in GBS adult diseases (Huber et al., 2011; Martins et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Huber et al., 2011 and Martins et al., 2012.

claim: CC17 GBS is largely underrepresented in GBS adult diseases.
source: Remarkably, this clone is less responsible for EOD and largely underrepresented in GBS adult diseases (Huber et al., 2011; Martins et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Huber et al., 2011 and Martins et al., 2012.

claim: Neonatal circulating concentrations of estradiol and progesterone at birth are more than 500 times superior to those of a male adult.
source: This hormonal exposure leads to neonatal circulating concentrations at birth which are more than 500 times superior to those of a male adult (Lagiou et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lagiou et al., 2014.

claim: Estradiol and progesterone levels drop during the first 3 days of life to stabilize for several months at concentrations still 5 to 50 times higher than those of an adult.
source: These levels drop during the first 3 days of life to stabilize for several months at concentrations still 5 to 50 times higher than those of an adult (Khashana et al., 2016; Kuijper et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Khashana et al., 2016 and Kuijper et al., 2013.

claim: Sex hormones modulate the immune response in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Interestingly, sex hormones modulate the immune response and the permeability of cellular barriers in a dose-dependent manner (Hata et al., 2014; Kovats, 2015; Robinson and Klein, 2012; Straub, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Sex hormones modulate the permeability of cellular barriers in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Interestingly, sex hormones modulate the immune response and the permeability of cellular barriers in a dose-dependent manner (Hata et al., 2014; Kovats, 2015; Robinson and Klein, 2012; Straub, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: CC17 GBS bacterial counts in the brain were approximately 10-fold higher in C7 mice compared to C0 and control mice at 2 and 24 hr after infection.
source: Mice subsequent gavage by 2.1010 colony forming units (CFU) of CC17 GBS led to higher bacterial counts (~10 fold) in the brain of C7 mice, 2 and 24 hr after infection, compared to C0 and control mice (Figure 1b)
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: CC23 GBS infection did not show any significant difference in brain bacterial counts between the 3 groups of mice.
source: In contrast, the same experiment using CC23 GBS did not show any significant difference between the 3 groups of mice
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: CC23 GBS showed lower CFU counts in the brain compared to CC17-infected C7 mice.
source: and lower CFU counts in the brain of CC23 compared to CC17-infected C7 mice (Figure 1b)
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: CC17 GBS and CC23 GBS growth in vitro was not altered by E2-P4 concentrations.
source: CC17 GBS and CC23 GBS growth in vitro was not altered by E2-P4 concentrations (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is demonstrated by growth curve data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: CC17 bacterial counts in the MLN were increased approximately 10-fold in C7 mice compared to C0 and control mice 2 hr after infection.
source: Besides, CC17 bacterial counts in the MLN and in the blood 2 hr after infection were increased ~10 fold in C7 mice in comparison to C0 and control mice (Figure 1c)
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: CC17 bacterial counts in the blood were increased approximately 10-fold in C7 mice compared to C0 and control mice 2 hr after infection.
source: Besides, CC17 bacterial counts in the MLN and in the blood 2 hr after infection were increased ~10 fold in C7 mice in comparison to C0 and control mice (Figure 1c)
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: No bacteria could be detected 24 hr after infection in the MLN, spleen, and blood.
source: However, no bacteria could be detected 24 hr after infection (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), indicating early digestive translocation and dissemination, followed by efficient bacterial clearance.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The enhanced invasiveness of CC17 GBS in E2-P4 C7 mice was associated with a stronger inflammatory response compared to C0 and control mice.
source: The enhanced invasiveness of CC17 GBS in E2-P4 C7 mice was associated with a stronger inflammatory response compared to C0 and control mice as indicated by the increased circulating levels of several cytokines including the interleukins IL-1ß and IL-10, and the leukocytes chemoattractant proteins CCL20 and CXCL2 which are secreted by epithelial and immune cells, respectively (Ranasinghe and Eri, 2018) (Figure 1d).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cytokine measurement data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: Bacteremia following intravenous infection was not statistically different between C0, C7, and control mice at 2 hr, 24 hr and 48 hr after infection.
source: The resulting bacteremia (Figure 1e) and total CFU counts in the spleen (Figure 1f) and brain (Figure 1g) were not statistically different between C0, C7, and control mice, 2 hr, 24 hr and 48 hr after infection
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figures 1e-g.

claim: Total CFU counts in the spleen following intravenous infection were not statistically different between C0, C7, and control mice at 2 hr, 24 hr and 48 hr after infection.
source: The resulting bacteremia (Figure 1e) and total CFU counts in the spleen (Figure 1f) and brain (Figure 1g) were not statistically different between C0, C7, and control mice, 2 hr, 24 hr and 48 hr after infection
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figures 1e-g.

claim: Total CFU counts in the brain following intravenous infection were not statistically different between C0, C7, and control mice at 2 hr, 24 hr and 48 hr after infection.
source: The resulting bacteremia (Figure 1e) and total CFU counts in the spleen (Figure 1f) and brain (Figure 1g) were not statistically different between C0, C7, and control mice, 2 hr, 24 hr and 48 hr after infection
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figures 1e-g.

claim: Neither bacterial clearance nor bacterial crossing of the BBB were affected by the hormonal conditions tested.
source: showing that neither bacterial clearance nor bacterial crossing of the BBB were affected by the hormonal conditions tested.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of differences in bacteremia and organ CFU counts following intravenous infection.

claim: Similar levels of tissue-associated bacteria were observed in C0, C7, and control mice following oral infection by CC17 GBS.
source: Following oral infection by CC17 GBS, similar levels of tissue-associated bacteria were observed in C0, C7, and control mice (Figure 2a)
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: A stronger invasion of the intestine and the Peyer's patches was seen in C7 mice.
source: but a stronger invasion of the intestine and the Peyer's patches was seen in C7 mice (Figure 2b)
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: M cells represent approximately 10% of the cells within the follicle-associated epithelium (FAE).
source: This process is achieved by microfold cells, also referred to as M cells, which represent approx. 10% of the cells within the FAE.
evidence: This is established knowledge about M cell distribution.

claim: M cells provide an efficient delivery of microorganisms and antigens to the underlying mucosal tissue.
source: M cells provide an efficient delivery of microorganisms and antigens to the underlying mucosal tissue, which contains an assorted population of lymphocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells (DC) (Mabbott et al., 2013; Nakamura et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mabbott et al., 2013 and Nakamura et al., 2018.

claim: CC17 GBS was observed associated with M cells in intestinal ligated loops.
source: Using confocal microscopy imaging of mouse intestinal ligated loops infected by CC17 GBS, we observed both M cells-associated bacteria (Figure 2c)
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images shown in Figure 2c.

claim: CC17 GBS was observed associated with CD11c positive cells in intestinal ligated loops.
source: and bacteria associated with CD11c positive cells, CD11c being a marker for macrophages and DC (Figure 2d–e).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images shown in Figures 2d-e.

claim: Intestinal mRNA levels of CCL20 and CCR6 were increased in E2-P4 C7 mice compared to C0 and control mice.
source: Besides, consistent with the elevated circulating levels of the chemokine CCL20 observed in E2-P4 C7 mice (Figure 1d), intestinal mRNA levels of the genes encoding the chemokine CCL20 and its cognate receptor C-C motif chemokine receptor 6 (CCR6) which are involved in leucocytes recruitment to the epithelium were also increased in E2-P4 C7 mice compared to C0 and control mice (Figure 2f).
evidence: This is demonstrated by gene expression data shown in Figure 2f.

claim: Genes involved in DC migration (Ccl19, Ccl21, Ccr7) were overexpressed approximately 2-fold in the intestinal tissue of E2-P4 C7 compared to C0 and control mice.
source: In parallel, genes expressed by immune cells and involved in DC migration to secondary lymph nodes, including the chemokines encoding genes Ccl19 and Ccl21 and their receptor Ccr7 involved in DC migration (Riol-Blanco et al., 2005), were overexpressed ~2 fold in the intestinal tissue of E2-P4 C7 compared to C0 and control mice (Figure 2g).
evidence: This is demonstrated by gene expression data shown in Figure 2g.

claim: There was a higher proportion of CD11c and MHC-II positive cells in the MLN of E2-P4 C7 mice.
source: This overexpression of DC activation and migration markers was associated with a higher proportion in the MLN of E2-P4 C7 mice of cells positive for CD11c and class II major histocompatibility complex (MHC-II) which are markers of activated DC (Figure 2h).
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2h.

claim: Adherence and invasion of CC17 GBS to Caco-2 enterocytes was not modified by E2-P4 concentrations.
source: Adherence and invasion of the CC17 GBS was not modified by E2-P4 concentrations (Figure 3a)
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: CC17 GBS was unable to cross the enterocytes monolayer whatever the hormonal condition tested.
source: and the bacterial counts in the lower compartment of the cell culture chamber up to 8 hr after enterocytes infection by their apical side were always below the detection limit, indicating that the bacteria were unable to cross the enterocytes monolayer whatever the hormonal condition tested.
evidence: This is demonstrated by transcytosis assay data.

claim: CC17 GBS could cross the epithelial layer composed of enterocytes and M cells.
source: In this co-culture system, CC17 GBS could cross the epithelial layer, as assessed by the percentage of transcytosis obtained 2 hr after infection (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is demonstrated by transcytosis assay data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: The transcytosis of CC17 GBS was potentiated approximately 2-fold in E2-P4 C7 condition compared to C0 and control conditions.
source: Furthermore, the transcytosis was potentiated approx. 2-fold in E2-P4 C7 condition in comparison to C0 and control (no hormones) conditions
evidence: This is demonstrated by transcytosis assay data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: CC17 GBS was more adherent to intestinal epithelial cells than CC23 GBS.
source: Thereby, we confirmed as previously described (Tazi et al., 2010) that CC17 GBS was more adherent to intestinal epithelial cells than CC23 GBS (Figure 3d–e)
evidence: This is demonstrated by adherence assay data shown in Figures 3d-e and supported by citation to Tazi et al., 2010.

claim: Approximately 50% of the cell-associated CC17 GBS were associated with M cells.
source: and more interestingly, we observed that approx. 50% of the cell-associated CC17 GBS were actually associated with M cells, either as adherent or intracellular bacteria (Figure 3f–g)
evidence: This is demonstrated by quantitative imaging analysis shown in Figures 3f-g.

claim: CC23 GBS were at 90% associated with enterocytes.
source: in contrast to CC23 GBS, which were at 90% associated with enterocytes (Figure 3f and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by quantitative imaging analysis shown in Figure 3f and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The proportion of M cells-associated CC17 GBS was approximately 50% higher in E2-P4 C7 than in C0 and control conditions.
source: Besides, the proportion of M cells-associated CC17 GBS was ~50% higher in E2-P4 C7 than in C0 and control conditions (Figure 3h)
evidence: This is demonstrated by quantitative imaging analysis shown in Figure 3h.

claim: RANKL mRNA levels in Raji B lymphocytes were three times higher in E2-P4 C7 condition than in E2-P4 C0 and control conditions.
source: Therefore, we measured the expression of RANKL in the Raji B lymphocytes used for M cells differentiation in vitro and found that the mRNA levels were three times higher in E2-P4 C7 condition than in E2-P4 C0 and control conditions (Figure 4a).
evidence: This is demonstrated by gene expression data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: mRNA levels of Spi-B and its target genes (TNFAIP2, GP2) were increased 2- to 3-fold in E2-P4 C7 condition.
source: In parallel, in epithelial cells, mRNA levels of Spi-B and of its target genes involved in M cells differentiation (TNFAIP2, GP2) were also increased 2- to 3-fold in E2-P4 C7 condition (Figure 4b)
evidence: This is demonstrated by gene expression data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: GP2 expression at least doubled both at the transcriptional and at the protein level in E2-P4 C7 condition.
source: and GP2 expression at least doubled both at the transcriptional and at the protein level (Figure 4b–d).
evidence: This is demonstrated by gene expression and Western blot data shown in Figures 4b-d.

claim: mRNA levels of murine Rankl, Spib and Gp2 were increased 2- to 3-fold in C7 condition compared to C0 and control condition in Peyer's patches.
source: In agreement with the results obtained in vitro, mRNA levels of murine Rankl, Spib and Gp2 were increased 2- to 3-fold in C7 condition compared to C0 and control condition (Figure 4e).
evidence: This is demonstrated by gene expression data shown in Figure 4e.

claim: Both HvgA and Srr2 contribute to GBS adherence to the intestinal epithelial cells in E2-P4 C7 condition.
source: Using ∆srr2 and ∆hvgA inactivated mutants, we first analyzed bacterial adherence to the enterocytes + M cells monolayer and showed that both HvgA and Srr2 contribute to GBS adherence to the intestinal epithelial cells in E2-P4 C7 condition (Figure 5a).
evidence: This is demonstrated by adherence assay data with mutants shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Only Srr2 was involved in CC17 GBS association with M cells.
source: Nevertheless, only Srr2 was involved in CC17 GBS association with M cells as objectified by quantitative image analysis which showed a 50% reduction in the association of the ∆srr2 mutant with GP2 positive cells in comparison to the wild-type (WT) strain and to the reverted mutant (back to WT, BTWT) isolate (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is demonstrated by quantitative imaging analysis shown in Figure 5b.

claim: The transcytosis capacity of the ∆srr2 mutant across the enterocytes + M cells monolayer was drastically impaired.
source: In agreement with these results, the transcytosis capacity of the ∆srr2 mutant across the enterocytes + M cells monolayer was drastically impaired (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is demonstrated by transcytosis assay data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: Srr2 contributes to CC17 GBS association with Peyer's patches.
source: The results clearly indicate that Srr2 contributes to CC17 GBS association with Peyer's patches (Figure 5d)
evidence: This is demonstrated by bacterial enumeration data in Peyer's patches shown in Figure 5d.

claim: Srr2 contributes to Peyer's patches invasion by CC17 GBS.
source: to Peyer's patches invasion (Figure 5e)
evidence: This is demonstrated by intratissular bacterial enumeration data shown in Figure 5e.

claim: Srr2 contributes to CC17 GBS dissemination to the MLN.
source: to dissemination to the MLN (Figure 5f)
evidence: This is demonstrated by bacterial enumeration data in MLN shown in Figure 5f.

claim: Srr2 contributes to CC17 GBS central nervous system invasion.
source: and to central nervous system invasion (Figure 5g).
evidence: This is demonstrated by bacterial enumeration data in brain shown in Figure 5g.

claim: Infection by the ∆srr2 mutant did not lead to higher bacterial counts in C7 mice than in C0 mice.
source: Furthermore, in contrast to infection by the WT CC17 GBS, infection by the ∆srr2 mutant did not lead to higher bacterial counts in C7 mice than in C0 mice (Figure 5c–f)
evidence: This is demonstrated by bacterial enumeration data shown in Figures 5c-f.

claim: Srr2 participates to the increased virulence of CC17 GBS in E2-P4 C7 hormonal condition.
source: suggesting that Srr2 participates to the increased virulence of CC17 GBS in E2-P4 C7 hormonal condition.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the ∆srr2 mutant does not show enhanced virulence in C7 condition.

claim: M cells are necessary for CC17 GBS crossing of intestinal epithelial cells in vitro.
source: Indeed, M cells are necessary for CC17 GBS crossing of intestinal epithelial cells in vitro, indicating that the preferential invasion route for CC17 GBS in this cellular model is transcytosis through M cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that CC17 GBS cannot cross enterocyte monolayers but can cross enterocyte + M cell monolayers.

claim: The preferential invasion route for CC17 GBS in the cellular model is transcytosis through M cells.
source: Indeed, M cells are necessary for CC17 GBS crossing of intestinal epithelial cells in vitro, indicating that the preferential invasion route for CC17 GBS in this cellular model is transcytosis through M cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing M cell-dependent transcytosis.

claim: Transcytosis is potentiated by E2-P4 hormonal conditions encountered in over 7 day-old neonates in correlation with a better M cell maturation in vitro and in vivo.
source: Transcytosis is potentiated by E2-P4 hormonal conditions encountered in over 7 day-old neonates in correlation with a better M cell maturation in vitro and in vivo and a higher CC17 GBS association with M cells in vitro.
evidence: This is demonstrated by transcytosis assays and M cell differentiation marker expression data.

claim: CC17 GBS exploits M cells to invade the host and reach the lymphatic system to disseminate.
source: Thus, we identified a cellular pathway for CC17 GBS intestinal translocation and showed that CC17 GBS exploits M cells to invade the host and reach the lymphatic system to disseminate.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that CC17 GBS crosses the intestinal barrier through M cells in Peyer's patches and reaches the MLN.

claim: GBS – M cells interaction is specific to the hypervirulent CC17 clone.
source: Importantly, we also demonstrate that GBS – M cells interaction is specific to the hypervirulent CC17 clone and mediated by the surface protein Srr2
evidence: This is demonstrated by the observation that CC17 GBS associates with M cells at much higher rates than CC23 GBS.

claim: GBS – M cells interaction is mediated by the surface protein Srr2.
source: Importantly, we also demonstrate that GBS – M cells interaction is specific to the hypervirulent CC17 clone and mediated by the surface protein Srr2
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments with ∆srr2 mutants showing reduced M cell association.

claim: Srr2 is always and almost exclusively present in GBS isolates belonging to the hypervirulent CC17 clone.
source: Because the surface protein Srr2 is always and almost exclusively present in GBS isolates belonging to the highly homogenous hypervirulent CC17 clone (Brochet et al., 2006; Da Cunha et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Brochet et al., 2006 and Da Cunha et al., 2014.

claim: CC17 GBS invasiveness depends on its ability to cross the intestinal barrier through M cells.
source: and because CC17 GBS invasiveness depends on its ability to cross the intestinal barrier through M cells
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that M cell transcytosis is necessary for CC17 GBS invasiveness.

claim: The increased virulence of the WT CC17 in E2-P4 C7 condition is Srr2 dependent.
source: suggesting that the increased virulence of the WT CC17 in this condition is Srr2 dependent.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the ∆srr2 mutant does not show enhanced virulence in C7 condition.

claim: Mouse oral gavage with 1.10^10 CFU of CC17 GBS was associated with 60% mortality in the 12 hr following infection in a previous study.
source: Notably, mouse oral gavage with 1.1010 CFU was associated with 60% mortality in the 12 hr following infection.
evidence: This is a reference to previous work by the authors.

claim: Mice gavage with 2.10^10 CFU did not lead to any mortality for up to 24 hr in any of the 3 groups of mice in the current study.
source: Conversely, in this work, mice gavage with 2.1010 CFU did not lead to any mortality for up to 24 hr in any of the 3 groups of mice
evidence: This is an observation from the current study.

claim: The difference in mortality between the previous and current study was not attributable to the hormonal treatments but more likely to the age of the mice at the time of infection.
source: indicating that the difference between these two models was not attributable to the hormonal treatments but more likely to the age of the mice at the time of infection.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of the two studies.

claim: CC17 GBS reaches the brain more efficiently in the first hours following oral than intravenous infection despite similar levels of bacteremia in both models.
source: Another interesting feature of the animal models used in this work resides in CC17 GBS capacity to reach the brain more efficiently in the first hours following oral than intravenous infection despite similar levels of bacteremia in both models (Figure 1).
evidence: This is observed from the data presented in Figure 1.

claim: After intravenous injection in the tail vein, the vast majority of bacteria is captured by the spleen and the liver.
source: After intravenous injection in the tail vein, bacteria reach the inferior vena cava (Cook, 1965) and the vast majority of them is then captured by the spleen and the liver.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cook, 1965 and is established knowledge about bacterial dissemination.

claim: When bacteria disseminate through the lymphatic vessels after reaching the MLN following oral infection, they eventually reach the blood circulation via the thoracic duct directly in the subclavian vein, thereby shunting the hepatic portal system.
source: Conversely, when bacteria disseminate through the lymphatic vessels after they got to the MLN following oral infection, they eventually reach the blood circulation via the thoracic duct directly in the subclavian vein, thereby shunting the hepatic portal system (Hsu and Itkin, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hsu and Itkin, 2016.

claim: CC17 GBS preferentially disseminates via the lymphatic system following oral infection.
source: These major differences are objectivized by the bacterial loads in the spleen following these 2 modes of infection (Figure 1) and reinforce the hypothesis that CC17 GBS preferentially disseminates via the lymphatic system following oral infection.
evidence: This is inferred from the differences in bacterial loads in the spleen between oral and intravenous infection routes.

claim: hvgA and srr2 represent the only surface proteins encoding genes that are always and almost exclusively expressed by the hypervirulent clone.
source: Among these, hvgA and srr2 represent the only surface proteins encoding genes that are always and almost exclusively expressed by the hypervirulent clone.
evidence: This is based on comparative genomics data.

claim: Both HvgA and Srr2 promote CC17 GBS adherence to a wide variety of cells including brain endothelial cells.
source: Both proteins promote CC17 GBS adherence to a wide variety of cells including brain endothelial cells and are involved in BBB crossing (Seo et al., 2013; Six et al., 2015; Tazi et al., 2010)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Seo et al., 2013, Six et al., 2015, and Tazi et al., 2010.

claim: Both HvgA and Srr2 are involved in BBB crossing.
source: Both proteins promote CC17 GBS adherence to a wide variety of cells including brain endothelial cells and are involved in BBB crossing (Seo et al., 2013; Six et al., 2015; Tazi et al., 2010)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Seo et al., 2013, Six et al., 2015, and Tazi et al., 2010.

claim: HvgA confers gut colonization capacities in murine models.
source: Besides, HvgA confers gut colonization capacities in murine models and it was presumed that CC17 GBS association with LOD was related to an increased ability of CC17 GBS to colonize neonates compared to other GBS clones (Tazi et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tazi et al., 2010.

claim: A recent large prospective cohort study showed that CC17 GBS was associated with a higher risk of delayed post-delivery colonization instead of colonizing neonates more efficiently than other GBS clones.
source: However, a recent large prospective cohort study of infant colonization by GBS showed that instead of colonizing neonates more efficiently than other GBS clones, CC17 GBS was associated with a higher risk of delayed post-delivery colonization (Tazi et al., 2019).
